title: Acoustic monitoring of solitary bee activity at nesting boxes
content:
A solitary bee (Osmia cornuta) exiting the nest box. The spectrogram shows a typical pattern for a flight buzzing sound.


Abstract

Monitoring of pollinator activity is of high interest in both agriculture and biodiversity and conservation studies. Passive acoustic monitoring has become increasingly popular because of its rather simple deployment and scalability, though challenges with data analysis remain. In this paper, we present a study on acoustic monitoring of solitary bees at nesting boxes. Within the framework of a citizen science project, volunteers set up 10 dedicated nesting boxes and recorded the soundscape several times per week using portable USB microphones. A neural network-based algorithm was developed to detect flight buzzing sounds in the recordings, allowing us to identify bee activity. The algorithm was evaluated for robustness and further validated in combination with simultaneous video recordings. The obtained F1-scores were 95.4 ± 1.2% and 89.3 ± 5.5% in the cross-validation and leave-one-location-out experiments, respectively. Practical implication. This approach allows us to monitor patterns of bee nesting activity over time, space, and environmental conditions. We suggest that with relatively minor adjustments the algorithm and sensors can be applied to a broad range of research questions on activity for not only solitary bees but also other groups of insects.

Povzetek

Spremljanje dejavnosti opraševalcev je pomembno tako v kmetijstvu kot v raziskavah biotske raznolikosti in ohranjanja okolja. Pasivno spremljanje na podlagi zvoka postaja vedno bolj zanimivo, ker se mikrofone lahko enostavno namesti, izziv pa predstavlja predvsem analiza podatkov. V članku predstavimo raziskavo spremljanja čebel samotark v gnezdilnicah na podlagi zvoka. V okviru projekta občanske znanosti so prostovoljci postavili deset namenskih gnezdilnic in večkrat na teden s prenosnim mikrofonom snemali zvok. Za analizo podatkov smo razvili algoritem, temelječ na nevronski mreži, ki prepozna zvoke brenčanja med letom in nam tako omogoči spremljanje dejavnosti čebel. Ocenili smo robustnost algoritma ter ga dodatno preverili s pomočjo simultanega video posnetka. Mera F1, ki jo je algoritem dosegel pri prečnem preverjanju, je bila 95,4 ± 1,2 %. Pri poskusu, kjer smo izvedli preizkus na lokaciji, ki ni bila uporabljena pri treniranju algoritma, je znašala 89,3 ± 5,5 %. Praktična uporaba: Naša metoda omogoča spremljanje dejavnosti gnezdenja čebel skozi čas, na različnih lokacijah in v različnih okoljskih pogojih. Z majhnimi prilagoditvami se lahko algoritem in senzor prilagodita na širok spekter raziskovalnih problemov povezanih z dejavnostjo ne le čebel samotark, ampak tudi drugih skupin žuželk.
